edition.window: Judgments and orders passed between 10:00 AM IST on 24 September 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 25 September 2026
edition.next: Next edition: tomorrow at 10:00 AM IST

highlights.text: No automatic arrest when a parent is accused under POCSO in a custody fight; a child psychiatrist must be consulted first.

highlights.caseName: Waris v. State of Madhya Pradesh
highlights.text: Death sentence for the rape-murder of a 6-year-old stepdaughter commuted to life imprisonment.

highlights.caseName: Danam Nagender v. Alleti Maheshwar Reddy
highlights.text: Telangana MLA Danam Nagender's disqualification for defection upheld.

highlights.caseName: Union of India v. Rohith Nathan & Anr.
highlights.text: Verdict reserved on the Centre's plea to make the OBC creamy-layer ruling prospective.
Anticipatory bail refused to Ajeet Bharti; video prima facie caste-based abuse of MP Chandrashekhar Azad.
Hate speech case against Annamalai quashed; criminal law is no tool to stifle political dissent.

items.caseName: 'R' v. 'E' & Anr. (and connected matters)
items.headline: Safeguards against misuse of POCSO in custody fights
items.text: Where a parent is accused under POCSO during a matrimonial dispute, there is no automatic arrest on an FIR and a child psychiatrist or psychologist must be consulted first. The Court quashed a mother's FIR against the father, which the CBI found unsupported, and asked the Family Court to oversee the child's return to him.
items.why: Police and courts now have national guardrails for POCSO complaints made in custody battles.

items.caseName: Waris v. State of Madhya Pradesh
items.coram: Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta & Vijay Bishnoi, JJ.
items.headline: Death sentence for rape-murder of 6-year-old commuted
items.text: The Court upheld the conviction for the rape and murder of the man's six-year-old stepdaughter. It set aside the death sentence and imposed life imprisonment, finding the case did not meet the test for capital punishment.

items.caseName: Danam Nagender v. Alleti Maheshwar Reddy
items.coram: Surya Kant, CJI, Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: Telangana MLA's defection disqualification upheld
items.text: The Court dismissed Danam Nagender's appeal against the Telangana High Court ruling disqualifying him as an MLA. He had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls on a Congress ticket while still a sitting BRS MLA.

items.caseName: Union of India & Ors. v. Ramdhani Prasad
items.coram: Aravind Kumar & Vipul M. Pancholi, JJ.
items.headline: Article 311 bar does not apply to an officer of equal rank
items.text: Article 311(1) only stops removal by an officer below the appointing authority's rank. An RPSF constable appointed by an Assistant Commandant was validly removed by an Adjutant of equal rank, so his removal was restored.

items.caseName: Naval Kishore & Anr. v. State of Punjab
items.coram: Aravind Kumar & Vipul M. Pancholi, JJ.
items.headline: Sessions courts cannot bar remission in a sentence
items.text: Only the Supreme Court and High Courts can impose a fixed-term or whole-life sentence that excludes remission. The Court replaced a trial court's no-remission life term with 25 years' rigorous imprisonment without remission.

items.caseName: Sri Anumandala Rajesh Reddy v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.headline: No sanction needed before a Magistrate orders an FIR
items.text: A Magistrate's direction under Section 156(3) CrPC to register an FIR comes before cognizance, so sanction under Section 197 to prosecute a public servant is not needed at that stage. The investigation, quashed by the High Court, will resume.

items.caseName: Union of India v. Rohith Nathan & Anr.
items.headline: Verdict reserved on making OBC creamy-layer ruling prospective
items.text: The Centre wants the March 2026 ruling, that creamy-layer status cannot rest on parents' salary alone, to leave completed recruitments and admissions untouched. The Court reserved its decision.

items.caseName: Mamata Banerjee v. Election Commission of India
items.coram: Surya Kant, CJI, Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: ECI told to propose a timeline in the Trinamool symbol dispute
items.text: The Court asked the Election Commission to suggest a timeframe for deciding the rival claims to the AITC name and symbol, fair to both sides but not drawn out. The matter is listed next week.

items.caseName: State of Tamil Nadu v. State of Karnataka
items.coram: Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta & Vijay Bishnoi, JJ.
items.headline: Karnataka to answer TN's Cauvery shortfall plea
items.text: Tamil Nadu says Karnataka has under-released Cauvery water by about 16–20 TMC. Karnataka has a week to reply, and the matter is listed in October.

items.caseName: Deepak Singla v. Directorate of Enforcement
items.coram: Surya Kant, CJI, Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: Notice to ED on AAP leader's bail plea
items.text: Deepak Singla challenges the Punjab & Haryana High Court's 9 September refusal of bail in a money-laundering case. The Court issued notice to the ED.

items.caseName: Sujay Radhakrishna Vikhe-Patil v. Nilesh Dyandev Lanke
items.coram: Surya Kant, CJI, Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana, JJ.
items.headline: Notice on challenge to Ahmednagar MP's 2024 win
items.text: The appeal challenges the Bombay High Court's dismissal of an election petition alleging corrupt practices and excess spending. The Court sought MP Nilesh Lanke's reply.

items.caseName: Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors.
items.coram: J.B. Pardiwala & K. Vinod Chandran, JJ.
items.headline: Last chance to Centre on online child abuse material
items.text: The IT and Law Ministries were given one last chance to report on implementing the 2024 judgment on child sexual abuse material and on safeguards for social media platforms. Next hearing: 15 October.

items.caseName: Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. v. V. Rajamani & Anr.
items.coram: J.B. Pardiwala & K. Vinod Chandran, JJ.
items.headline: Execution rules for commercial suits should be in the statute
items.text: The Court suggested adding a Schedule of execution rules to the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 to tackle pending execution petitions. It awaits fresh data from the High Courts; next date 7 October.

items.caseName: Siddharth Varadarajan v. State of U.P. & Anr.
items.headline: The Wire editor allowed to travel to the US
items.text: The court let Siddharth Varadarajan travel to New York from 28 September to 7 October. It noted the trial in the 2020 FIRs has not begun and found nothing to suggest he would abscond.

items.caseName: Shahrukh v. State of U.P. (with connected jail appeal)
items.coram: Siddhartha Varma & Jai Krishna Upadhyay, JJ.
items.headline: Call records alone can't place accused with the victim
items.text: The court acquitted a wife and her alleged partner of her husband's murder. Call detail records by themselves do not prove the accused were physically with the deceased, and the chain of circumstances was incomplete.

items.caseName: Ashok Maruti Kanase v. State of Maharashtra
items.headline: Creating a situation that drives suicide can be abetment
items.text: The court upheld a husband's conviction for cruelty and abetting his wife's suicide after harassment over money. Abetment can include creating circumstances that amount to instigation.

items.caseName: Milan Pradhan v. State of West Bengal
items.headline: Nandigram by-poll candidate protected in a 2007 case
items.text: Police may take no further steps against the Congress candidate in a 2007 case until 12 October. The court was surprised the police acted only now, 19 years later, just before the by-poll.

items.caseName: Ishani Datta Ray & Anr. v. State of West Bengal & Ors.
items.headline: No coercive action against ABP journalists over headline FIR
items.text: The court protected an Anandabazar Patrika editor and journalist from coercive action until 15 December over the 'Gerua Gundami' headline, provided they keep cooperating with the probe.

items.caseName: Ajeet Bharti v. State
items.headline: Anticipatory bail refused in SC/ST Act case
items.text: The court found Ajeet Bharti's video prima facie used caste superiority to humiliate MP Chandrashekhar Azad, disclosing offences under the SC/ST Act. That Act bars anticipatory bail.

items.caseName: Dr. Manish Kamra v. Union of India & Ors.
items.headline: Higher education can't be curtailed lightly
items.text: A government doctor was allowed leave for a three-year cardiology super-speciality course. The right to higher education is not a fundamental right, but it cannot be restricted without good reason.

items.caseName: Omar Rashid v. X & Ors.
items.headline: Notice on journalist's plea against anonymous posts
items.text: The court issued notice on journalist Omar Rashid's plea to take down anonymous posts accusing him of sexual harassment. It remarked that serious allegations need corroboration. Listed on 7 October.

items.caseName: S v. Union of India & Ors.
items.headline: Adoptive mother's plea to hand son to CARA
items.text: A widowed adoptive mother seeks to transfer custody of her son to CARA or the Child Welfare Committee, citing behavioural issues. The court sought replies within a week.

items.caseName: Dr. Vikas Divyakirti v. Meta Platforms Inc. & Ors.
items.headline: Drishti IAS founder's personality rights suit
items.text: The suit seeks protection of Vikas Divyakirti's name and likeness, including against fake online profiles. The judge sent it to the bench hearing personality-rights cases.

items.caseName: Arvind Kejriwal v. Gujarat University & Ors.
items.coram: Sunita Agarwal, CJ & D.N. Ray, J.
items.headline: PM degree row: verdict reserved on Kejriwal's cost appeal
items.text: Kejriwal challenges the 2023 order that set aside the CIC's direction to disclose PM Modi's degree and made him pay ₹25,000 costs. The bench reserved judgment.

items.caseName: Imtiyaz Nuruddin Chinchali v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.headline: Insulting the PM is not an offence without intent to breach peace
items.text: Rude or abusive words alone do not attract Section 352 BNS without intent to provoke a breach of the peace. The court quashed the case against a shopkeeper.

items.caseName: R v. S
items.coram: D.K. Singh & H. Shanthi Bhushan, JJ.
items.headline: Short marriage alone doesn't fix alimony
items.text: The court upheld ₹50 lakh permanent alimony and dismissed both spouses' appeals. The length of a marriage cannot alone decide the amount.

items.caseName: Adaguru H. Vishwanath v. B.S. Suresha
items.headline: Defamation case against MLC over MUDA remarks continues
items.text: The court refused to quash defamation proceedings over press-conference remarks against a minister. Good faith and harm to reputation are questions for trial.

items.caseName: Yellamma & Ors. v. Ramappa & Ors.
items.headline: Presumption of a joint Hindu family weakens with distance
items.text: Seventy years of separate living rebutted the presumption that two branches of a family were still joint. A common ancestor alone is not enough.

items.caseName: Asma Ghori (Mogare) & Ors. v. State of Karnataka & Ors.
items.headline: Urdu and Marathi teachers' recruitment plea sent back
items.text: The bench sent back linguistic-minority candidates' challenge for a hearing on merits, recording the State's statement that it is considering recruiting Urdu and Marathi teachers.

items.caseName: Raeesa Parveen v. Union of India & Ors.
items.headline: No court decree needed to remove ex-husband's name from passport
items.text: Talaq is a valid divorce under Muslim personal law and the passport rules do not require a decree. The passport office must process the reissue without one.

items.caseName: Tomin J. Thachankary v. State of Kerala
items.headline: Verdict reserved on ex-DGP's plea to suspend sentence
items.text: The former DGP seeks suspension of his four-year sentence for disproportionate assets. The judge remarked that PC Act convicts are too easily released pending appeal, and reserved orders.

items.caseName: Annamalai K v. Piyush V
items.headline: Hate speech case against Annamalai quashed
items.text: Nothing showed intent to promote enmity in Annamalai's remarks about Muthuramalinga Thevar. The court warned against using criminal law to stifle political dissent.

items.caseName: V v. A
items.headline: 'If there are housewives, there can be house husbands'
items.text: The court dissolved an irretrievably broken marriage on the husband's offer of ₹2.5 crore for his wife and children. It observed that husbands taking up homemaking should become normal.

items.caseName: K. Suthan v. Union of India & Ors.
items.coram: S.A. Dharmadhikari, CJ & G. Arul Murugan, J.
items.headline: 'We cannot legislate': bye-poll cost PIL dismissed
items.text: The court dismissed a PIL seeking to recover bye-election costs from MLAs who resign soon after winning. Such a rule is for the legislature, not the courts.

items.caseName: State of Punjab v. Union of India & Ors.
items.headline: Punjab withdraws habeas plea after ED raid ends
items.text: After the ED search ended and the officials were freed, Punjab withdrew its habeas corpus plea with liberty to go to the proper forum. The State must pay the warrant officer's ₹55,000 fee.

items.court: Principal District & Sessions Court, Gandhinagar, Gujarat
items.caseName: Ravi Nair v. Government of Gujarat & Anr.
items.coram: Ashish J.S. Malhotra, Principal District & Sessions Judge
items.headline: Journalist Ravi Nair granted bail in Adani defamation case
items.text: The sessions court granted Ravi Nair regular bail. He had been arrested on a non-bailable warrant after missing a hearing in his appeal in the Adani defamation case.

items.caseName: Chhagan Chandrakant Bhujbal v. State of Maharashtra
items.headline: Chhagan Bhujbal discharged in Central Library case
items.text: The special court found no ground to proceed against the minister in the Kalina Central Library corruption case. Criminal liability needs proof of the accused's own participation, not 'invisible support'.
